original: Measurement presents itself as a procedure for establishing objective quantities, yet examination of practice reveals the deep imbrication of technique with interpretation. Instruments impose particular forms on phenomena, rendering some dimensions legible while occluding others; operational definitions select which aspects of complex wholes merit enumeration. The position that commands increasing assent holds that quantification represents a human choice about what to render countable rather than a neutral revelation of fact. Consequently, rigorous measurement practice must extend beyond the technical apparatus to encompass sustained reflection on the purposes embedded in one's choices.
